ai_policy_name: Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy
governing_body: African Union Commission (endorsed by the AU Executive Council)
governance_structure: AU Commission coordinates; member states implement nationally
main_motivation: Africa-centric, development-focused AI adoption aligned with Agenda 2063
description: A continental framework that guides AU member states on harnessing AI for development while managing risks. It is organised around five focus areas: capturing AI benefits, building capabilities, minimising risks, stimulating investment, and fostering cooperation. It is non-binding and intended to inform national strategies and regional harmonisation.

ai_policy_name: Disposición 2/2023 – Recomendaciones para una Inteligencia Artificial Fiable (Disposition 2/2023 – Recommendations for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence)
governing_body: Subsecretaría de Tecnologías de la Información, Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
governance_structure: Public-sector bodies apply the recommendations to their own AI projects
main_motivation: Ethical guidance for AI projects in the national public administration
description: Disposición 2/2023 approves a set of recommendations for trustworthy AI addressed to projects designed, developed or adopted by the national public sector, together with a diagram of the stages of an AI project. Aligned with the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, it emphasises human-centred design, transparency, human oversight, non-discrimination, data protection and accountability across the project lifecycle. It is guidance rather than a binding regulatory regime.
source_publisher: Argentina.gob.ar (Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros)

milestones.title: Published in the Boletín Oficial

notes: Signed 1 June 2023, published 2 June 2023. Both official pages fetched successfully.

ai_policy_name: Decisión Administrativa 899/2024 – Mesa Interministerial sobre Inteligencia Artificial (Administrative Decision 899/2024 – Interministerial Board on Artificial Intelligence)

description: This administrative decision restructures the Interministerial Board on AI originally created in 2023, placing it under the presidency of the Secretariat of Innovation, Science and Technology and expanding its membership to ministries including Defence, Economy, Foreign Affairs, Health, Security, Human Capital, Justice and State Deregulation. The board is tasked with coordinating the government's approach to AI adoption across economic and social sectors and with developing national strategies. Argentina has not yet adopted a standalone national AI strategy or a binding AI law.
source_publisher: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina

milestones.title: Decisión Administrativa 899/2024 published in the Boletín Oficial

ai_policy_name: Voluntary AI Safety Standard
governing_body: National Artificial Intelligence Centre (Department of Industry, Science and Resources)
governance_structure: National AI Centre publishes and maintains; adoption by organisations is voluntary
main_motivation: Give Australian organisations practical, internationally aligned guardrails for safe AI use
description: The Voluntary AI Safety Standard sets out ten voluntary guardrails for organisations across the AI supply chain, covering accountability, risk management, data governance, testing, human oversight, transparency, contestability and record-keeping, and shows through examples how developers and deployers should apply them. Its language is aligned with international AI management standards. In October 2025 the government issued simplified Guidance for AI Adoption with six essential practices, which evolves and supersedes the standard.
source_publisher: Department of Industry, Science and Resources

description: These measures govern generative AI services offered to the public in China, whether producing text, images, audio or video. Providers must use lawfully sourced training data, take steps against discrimination, protect personal information, label generated content, handle user complaints and ensure outputs comply with content rules. Services with public-opinion or social-mobilisation capacity must complete security assessments and algorithm filing. The measures took effect on 15 August 2023.

ai_policy_name: Measures for Labeling Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Synthetic Content
governing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China with MIIT, Ministry of Public Security and NRTA
governance_structure: Cyberspace Administration of China coordinates; enforced through algorithm filing and security assessment processes
main_motivation: Make AI-generated content identifiable to counter misinformation and misuse
description: These measures require providers of AI generation and synthesis services to attach explicit labels (visible text, audio or graphic notices) and implicit labels (embedded metadata) to generated text, images, audio, video and virtual scenes. Platforms distributing content must check for and preserve labels, users must declare AI-generated material, and removing or forging labels is prohibited. Compliance is checked during algorithm filing and security assessments. The measures took effect on 1 September 2025.

ai_policy_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
governing_body: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
governance_structure: AI Office within the European Commission (general-purpose AI models); national market surveillance authorities; European Artificial Intelligence Board
main_motivation: Risk-based product safety rules for AI to protect fundamental rights while enabling a single market for trustworthy AI
description: The AI Act is a binding EU regulation that sorts AI systems into risk tiers: a short list of prohibited practices, a set of high-risk uses subject to conformity, documentation, data-governance and human-oversight duties, transparency duties for limited-risk systems, and no specific rules for the rest. It adds a separate obligations regime for general-purpose AI models, overseen centrally by the Commission's AI Office. Application is staggered over several years after entry into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibitions applying from February 2025 and general-purpose model duties from August 2025.
source_publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex)

governance_structure: ETDA under MDES, with sectoral regulators envisaged
main_motivation: Consolidate earlier draft AI instruments into one risk-based AI law
description: Draft principles for a Thai AI law released for public hearing by MDES and ETDA. They propose a risk-based structure that distinguishes prohibited and high-risk AI, duties for providers and deployers, human oversight, incident reporting and a regulatory sandbox, while leaving sector regulators to set proportionate rules. The draft merges the 2022 ONDE royal decree draft and the 2023 ETDA promotion act draft.
source_publisher: Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA), Thailand

milestones.title: ETDA opens public hearing on draft AI law principles (comments to 24 June 2025)

notes: Date is the ETDA news item date (11 June B.E. 2568). Subsequent revision status after the 2025 hearing not confirmed from an official page.

ai_policy_name: UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (UAE National Strategy for AI 2031)
governing_body: UAE Government / Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence
governance_structure: UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence oversees implementation via committees and sub-councils
main_motivation: Make the UAE a global AI leader by 2031 as the first project of UAE Centennial 2071
description: Launched in October 2017, the strategy aims to embed AI across government services and priority sectors such as health, education, transport, energy and space, and to make the UAE a leading AI destination by 2031. Its objectives include AI-friendly legislation, talent development, research capability, data infrastructure and strong governance. The UAE Council for AI was created to drive implementation.
source_publisher: Official Platform of the UAE Government (u.ae)

ai_policy_name: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
governing_body: UAE Cabinet / Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
governance_structure: AI Office under the Minister of State for AI; applies across federal entities
main_motivation: Guiding principles for safe, ethical and inclusive AI aligned with the 2031 strategy
description: A twelve-principle charter approved by the UAE Cabinet setting expectations for AI development and use, including safety, algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency, human oversight, governance and accountability, and compliance with applicable laws and treaties. It is a guiding framework rather than binding legislation and supports the objectives of the UAE Strategy for AI.

ai_policy_name: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation
governing_body: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (with the Office for Artificial Intelligence)
governance_structure: Existing sectoral regulators apply five cross-cutting principles; central coordination function within DSIT
main_motivation: Regulate AI through existing regulators and principles rather than a new AI statute, to support innovation
description: This white paper sets out the UK government's framework for AI regulation, based on five cross-sector principles (safety and robustness, transparency and explainability, fairness, accountability and governance, contestability and redress) to be applied by existing regulators within their remits rather than through a single AI law. It proposes central government functions to monitor risks, support regulator coordination and run sandboxes. A consultation ran until June 2023, and the government response of February 2024 confirmed the approach while flagging that binding measures for highly capable general-purpose models may be needed later.
source_publisher: GOV.UK (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)

milestones.title: White paper published and consultation opened
Government response to the consultation published

notes: Status set to 'whitepaper' because the instrument is a white paper; the principles-based approach it describes is operative through regulators but no AI statute has been enacted.

ai_policy_name: AI Opportunities Action Plan
governing_body: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
governance_structure: DSIT leads delivery across government; recommendations adopted via the government response
main_motivation: Use AI to drive economic growth, public-service improvement and sovereign UK AI capability
description: The AI Opportunities Action Plan is an independent report by Matt Clifford commissioned by the government, containing 50 recommendations organised under three aims: laying foundations (compute, data, skills and regulation), driving AI adoption across the public and private sectors, and securing homegrown frontier AI capability. The government published a response accepting the recommendations and treats the plan as its roadmap for AI-led growth.
source_publisher: GOV.UK (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)

milestones.title: Action Plan and government response published

ai_policy_name: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
governing_body: Government Digital Service (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)
governance_structure: Government Digital Service; applied by departments and public bodies
main_motivation: Give civil servants practical rules for safe, lawful and effective use of AI in public services
description: The AI Playbook is official guidance for UK public-sector organisations on selecting, buying, building and deploying AI. It sets ten principles covering legality, security, human oversight, transparency and accountability, and explains AI capabilities, limitations and risks in plain terms. It expands and replaces the January 2024 Generative AI Framework for HMG to cover a broader range of AI technologies.
source_publisher: GOV.UK (Government Digital Service)

milestones.title: AI Playbook published, superseding the Generative AI Framework for HMG

ai_policy_name: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
governing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (US Department of Commerce)
governance_structure: NIST maintains the framework; adoption by organisations is voluntary
main_motivation: Give organisations a common, voluntary approach to identifying and managing AI risks
description: The AI RMF is a voluntary framework developed by NIST with public input to help organisations manage risks to individuals, organisations and society from AI systems. It defines characteristics of trustworthy AI and organises risk management into four functions: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage. NIST has since added companion resources, including a Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) in July 2024, and has stated that the framework is being revised in line with the 2025 AI Action Plan.
source_publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

milestones.title: AI RMF 1.0 released
Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) released

ai_policy_name: Executive Order 14179: Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence
governing_body: President of the United States (Executive Office of the President)
governance_structure: Assistant to the President for Science and Technology, AI and Crypto Czar and National Security Advisor coordinate; OMB revises agency AI memoranda
main_motivation: Reset federal AI policy toward deregulation and US global AI dominance
description: This executive order revokes Executive Order 14110 of October 2023 and declares a federal policy of sustaining US leadership in AI. It directs senior White House officials to produce an AI action plan within 180 days, orders a review of all actions taken under the revoked order with suspension or rescission of those found inconsistent, and requires OMB to revise its agency AI governance memoranda.
source_publisher: The White House

ai_policy_name: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
governing_body: The White House (Office of Science and Technology Policy)
governance_structure: OSTP coordinates; implementation assigned to federal departments and agencies
main_motivation: Secure US leadership in AI through deregulation, infrastructure build-out and export of American AI
description: America's AI Action Plan is the federal AI strategy mandated by Executive Order 14179. It lists more than 90 policy actions grouped under three pillars: accelerating innovation (including removing regulatory barriers), building AI infrastructure such as data centres and chip fabrication with streamlined permitting, and leading internationally through AI exports and security measures. It was released with accompanying executive orders on federal procurement, data-centre permitting and AI exports.
source_publisher: The White House

ai_policy_name: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial del Uruguay 2024-2030 (National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Uruguay 2024-2030)
governing_body: Agencia de Gobierno Electrónico y Sociedad de la Información y del Conocimiento (Agesic)
governance_structure: Agesic leads implementation under the Comité Estratégico del Sector Público para IA y Datos, with mid-term review and periodic progress reports
main_motivation: Ethical, sovereign AI development supporting sustainable growth
description: Uruguay's 2024-2030 strategy was approved on 21 November 2024 by the public-sector Strategic Committee for AI and Data after a participatory process involving more than 300 people from state bodies, civil society and the private sector, with technical support from CAF and UNESCO. It sets guiding principles and three objectives: governance and safeguards for ethical and safe AI, national capabilities in infrastructure, data and talent, and use of AI for sustainable development and better public services. A roadmap with goals and semi-annual reporting accompanies the strategy.

ai_policy_name: National Strategy on Research, Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence to 2030 (Decision No. 127/QD-TTg)
governing_body: Prime Minister of Vietnam
governance_structure: Ministry of Science and Technology as focal point coordinating 15+ ministries
main_motivation: Make Vietnam a leading AI centre in ASEAN and the world's top 50 by 2030
description: A prime ministerial decision promulgating Vietnam's national AI strategy to 2030. It targets a top-four ASEAN and top-50 global position in AI, three national big data and high-performance computing centres, national innovation centres for AI and open datasets across sectors. It directs work on a legal framework, infrastructure, talent and application of AI in government and industry, with the Ministry of Science and Technology coordinating.
source_publisher: Government of Vietnam legal document portal (vanban.chinhphu.vn)

ai_policy_name: Law on Artificial Intelligence (Law No. 134/2025/QH15)
governing_body: National Assembly of Vietnam
governance_structure: Government/Ministry of Science and Technology as state management body
main_motivation: Establish a comprehensive, risk-based legal framework for AI while promoting innovation
description: Vietnam's first dedicated AI statute, with eight chapters and 35 articles governing the research, development, provision, deployment and use of AI systems. It adopts a risk-based approach, requires human oversight in important decisions, and provides for national AI infrastructure, a national AI development fund, a regulatory sandbox and rules on AI-generated content. It took effect on 1 March 2026 with transition periods for existing systems.
source_publisher: Government of Vietnam legal document portal (vanban.chinhphu.vn)
